question: What did the actual customers say in the calls supporting that conclusion?

answer.answer_markdown:
**In their own words, customers are not complaining that they lost the argument - they are saying no argument took place: they sent the documents, and the refusal came back anyway.** Across the 379 calls behind this conclusion there are 717 verified verbatim statements and 381 distinct wordings of the problem, and they fall into four things customers keep saying.

The first is that the evidence did not matter. "Despite providing evidence, Chase denied my dispute, stating that the charge was valid because there was no record of a return." "Chase denied my dispute but : Did not provide me with a clear written explanation of the evidence relied upon." "I have already provided the bank ALL materials incuding the 'we quit '' letter, but the bank is still placing the purchases back onto my credit card account." One customer measured the gap directly: "The court, reviewing the same evidence, ruled in my favor within two hours."

The second is speed - the decision arrived too fast to have been an investigation. "I made a claim on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. It was closed within XXXX day." "the next morning in less than XXXX hours I was notified that the claims were closed even before I had time to upload evidence into the Chase claims portal." The third is the clock: "They said they couldnt do anything as it wasnt reported in 5 days. How could I report it when they insisted it went to the right place." And: "Chase would not open a claim and said the system was " built in a way that can not be overridden if it's been more than 65 days -- I reported it 7 days too late )." The fourth is the credit that is given and then taken back - "I then filed a dispute with my bank, Chase, which initially issued a provisional refund of $760.00, but later reversed it without any valid reason" - which customers experience as being told twice, with the second answer unexplained.

This is not one product's problem. Credit cards carry 169 of the calls, the highest rate of any product at 11.9% of credit card contacts; checking and savings carry 188, at 8.8%. The same sentences turn up in money transfers (15 calls), auto loans (3) and debt collection (3): "one of them went and zelled himself $500.00 I reported this to Chase and they are denying my claim saying it was sent from the same Ip address." And it is not recent: 165 of the calls fall in the first year of the window, July 2024 to June 2025, saying the same things. The full set of statements is attached below, spread over months and products.

quotes.why: January 2026, credit card. The single clearest statement of the theme: evidence in, denial out.

quotes.why: September 2025, credit card. The customer names the missing artefact: a written explanation of what the decision was based on.

quotes.quote: The court, reviewing the same evidence, ruled in my favor within two hours.
quotes.why: November 2024, credit card. The sharpest external benchmark a customer offers on the quality of the review.

quotes.why: February 2025, checking and savings, servicemember. Repeated rework with the same outcome.

quotes.quote: XXXX days later, they responded and said the purchases were authorized.
quotes.why: June 2026, checking and savings, the most recent month in the index. The pattern is still live.

quotes.quote: falsely stating that the amount had already been paid and subtracting costs for XXXX and XXXX, which were financed but not listed as exclusions in the contract
quotes.why: July 2025, auto loan. The same pattern on a protection claim, against the contract's own terms.

quotes.quote: one of them went and zelled himself $500.00 I reported this to Chase and they are denying my claim saying it was sent from the same Ip address
quotes.why: April 2026, money transfer. A single automated signal - the IP address - used to refuse the whole claim.

quotes.quote: Chase initially credited my account but ultimately reversed the refund and denied my dispute, despite evidence that the company was not fulfilling their obligations in accordance with federal debt relief regulations.
quotes.why: November 2025, debt collection. Shows the theme reaching the smallest products in the index.

caveats: The index mixes two corpora: 4,425 real written CFPB complaints about one bank covering July 2024 to June 2026, and 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from September 2023 only. All but one of the statements here are written complaint text, so this is complaint prose, not call transcription.
XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX are the CFPB's own redactions of names, amounts and dates in the published narratives; they are in the source text, not something the pipeline removed.
Every quote is verified against the source document character by character, but the account it gives is the customer's. The bank's file may show evidence the customer did not see.
Quotes are selected for spread across months and products, not sampled at random, so their mix is not a frequency estimate of which wording is most common.
followups: How many of these customers say they had already been given a provisional credit that was later reversed, and what does that reversal cost us in repeat contacts?
Would sending the written explanation of evidence relied upon with every denial remove most of this volume, and which teams would have to produce it?

sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY n_calls DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id
